HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (DETAILED)

Consult Summary:
71-year-old man with sudden onset left-arm paralysis, left facial tingling, mild dysphasia and possible dysphagia beginning ~1 hour prior to call; emergency ambulance arranged for suspected acute cerebrovascular event.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Unable to move left arm on awakening 1 hour ago.  
• Course/timing: Symptoms began on waking; unchanged at time of call.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Tingling on left side of face since onset.  
  – Mild difficulty swallowing liquids (small spill) and slowed/effortful speech.  
  – No left-leg weakness.  
  – No facial asymmetry noted by patient.  
  – No pain, discoloration, or coldness in arm.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified.  
• Review of systems otherwise not discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – long-standing; current control not discussed.  
• Hypertension – on treatment.  
• No previous similar neurologic episodes.

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Losartan – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Amlodipine – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• Penicillin – reaction not specified.

Social History:
• Lives alone.  
• Former smoker (quantity/quit date not specified).  
• Alcohol: several pints of beer on weekends plus “a couple more” during the week.  
• No recreational drug use mentioned.

Family History:
• Father with heart disease; further details unknown.  
• No other familial illnesses reported.

Physical Examination:
(telephone consultation—findings patient-reported)  
• General: Alert, able to converse; speech slowed/effortful.  
• Neurologic: Complete motor inability to move left arm; left facial tingling; no leg symptoms reported.  
• No objective vitals, facial droop, or other findings available.

Investigations:
• None performed prior to transfer.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected acute ischemic stroke (left-sided weakness, facial paresthesia, dysphasia)  
  – Emergency ambulance dispatched to patient’s home.  
  – Instructed patient to unlock front door and wait in hallway for paramedics.  
  – Clinician remained on phone until EMS arrival.  
  – Anticipate ED stroke team evaluation, neuro-imaging, and reperfusion therapy assessment (tPA or thrombectomy) per protocol.

Issue 2: Chronic conditions (type 2 diabetes, hypertension)  
  – To be reviewed after acute event; current medications listed.

General Plan Items:  
  – Update primary care record with encounter details and hospital transfer.  
  – Encourage patient to inform next-of-kin once stable.

Quality checks:

• Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, full neurologic exam, medication doses/frequencies, last known well time confirmation, blood glucose reading, anticoagulant/bleeding history, allergy reaction details.  
• Internal conflicts: none noted.  
• Transcript quality: clear audio; minor pauses but clinically complete for emergency context.
